harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as the DNS forwarder for the shared 10.100.232.0/24 network using Ansible from control node node4. node1 answers inventory.internal with node2's address (10.100.232.11) via a VyOS static-host-mapping and forwards all other queries to the upstream resolver 10.100.232.1. node2 and node3 (Ubuntu 16.04) are configured via a resolvconf head override to resolve through node1. Implementation is a two-play Ansible playbook (/root/ansible-dns/playbook.yml on node4): play 1 uses raw VyOS configure-mode commands (wrapped in sudo bash -c, required because Ubuntu 16.04/VyOS lack a python3 new enough for standard ansible-core 2.21 modules) to set service dns forwarding + static-host-mapping and verifies local resolution; play 2 uses raw SSH commands to install /etc/resolvconf/resolv.conf.d/head with nameserver 10.100.232.10, regenerate resolv.conf, and verify both inventory.internal and a public name resolve. Verified idempotent re-runs. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured healthy baselines, restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time (native reboot), confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed DNS forwarding/config persistence and client resolution recovered on every node, including a full successful Ansible playbook re-run from node4 after its own reboot.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes: node1=VyOS router (DNS target), node2/node3=Ubuntu 16.04 (DNS clients), node4=Ubuntu 24.04 control node with ansible-core 2.21 pre-installed, all on shared 10.100.232.0/24
Set up passwordless SSH from node4 to node1 (vyos user, added via VyOS system login public-keys), node2 and node3 (antrieb user, appended cluster pubkey to authorized_keys)
Manually validated the exact VyOS DNS forwarding + static-host-mapping command sequence before automating it
Wrote Ansible inventory.ini, ansible.cfg, and playbook.yml on node4 under /root/ansible-dns
Diagnosed and fixed 'set -e' + pty interaction causing false failures on VyOS raw commands
Diagnosed and fixed ansible-core module f-string incompatibility with Ubuntu 16.04's Python 3.5.2 by switching client tasks to ansible.builtin.raw
Ran the playbook end-to-end, verified inventory.internal resolves to 10.100.232.11 and public names resolve via forwarding, from node1 and from node2/node3
Re-ran the playbook to confirm idempotency
Captured boot_id/service/data baselines on all 4 nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially via native reboot, polling each until reachable again
Confirmed changed boot_id on every node post-restart

Verified DNS forwarding config, static-host-mapping, and client resolv.conf/resolution all persisted and recovered after each restart, and re-ran the full Ansible playbook successfully from node4 after its own reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as DNS forwarder answering inventory.internal with node2's address and forwarding everything else upstream
evidence.summary: VyOS service dns forwarding + static-host-mapping applied and committed/saved via Ansible; dig confirms inventory.internal -> 10.100.232.11 and example.com resolves via upstream 10.100.232.1

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to resolve through node1, implemented via Ansible
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook run installs resolvconf head file pointing at 10.100.232.10 on both clients; getent hosts confirms inventory.internal and example.com resolve correctly through node1

evidence.requirement: Implementation performed via Ansible from the designated control node
evidence.summary: inventory.ini/ansible.cfg/playbook.yml created on node4 (control_node) and ansible-playbook executed from there against node1/node2/node3

evidence.requirement: node1 restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered DNS state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5bcff8f9...; reboot issued; post-reboot boot_id changed to 7bc5f980...; DNS forwarding config, static-host-mapping and resolution all confirmed working after restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered client DNS resolution
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2dffe735...; reboot issued; post-reboot boot_id changed to 780db765...; resolv.conf and inventory.internal/example.com resolution confirmed recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered client DNS resolution
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id dbb46974...; reboot issued; post-reboot boot_id changed to 81c263fd...; resolv.conf and resolution confirmed recovered

evidence.requirement: node4 (control node) restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered orchestration capability
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d3d54083...; reboot issued; post-reboot boot_id changed to e114543b...; full Ansible playbook re-run from node4 succeeded end-to-end after its own restart, proving orchestration capability recovered
